String: You overheard one of your them whisper "<This is so cringe/Watching paint dry would be more fun/This is the worst thing I've ever seen/I hate everything about this/Gag me with a spoon>".
Every single one of them rose to their feet and chanted your name at its conclusion.
Several of them said they've never been so moved by a piece of media.
They sprang to their feet and chanted "<honorific>" once it was over.
You heard <a smattering of laughter/inappropriate giggling/stifled laughter> after asking them what they thought of it.
Several of them exchanged awkward glances before leaving the room.
You caught several of your followers <making out/licking each others' ears/canoodling> instead of paying attention.
Several of them asked if they could be in the next production.
Some of them asked if they could <miss/skip/be excused from> the next one.

The majority of them remarked they'd rather watch <'The Room'/'Birdemic'/'Sharknado 4'/'Twilight'/paint dry/water boil/a turtle cross the road/the grass grow/C-SPAN/traffic court proceedings/a city council meeting/a town hall meeting/a political debate>.

You overheard a few of them say that not even '<Everything Everywhere All At Once/Avengers: Endgame/The Hunger Games/Titanic/Zoolander/The Breakfast Club/Heathers/Mean Girls/The Craft/Legally Blonde/Blair Witch Project>' could compete with it.
They said they'd give it a solid <C+/C-/C/two stars/two-and-a-half stars> if they had to rate it.
As they left, several of them said they wished it was longer.
They all began shouting that it needs a sequel.
Their reaction to it suggested the film was <not bad/sort of tepid/a bit meh/somewhere between just okay and good/a worthy effort>
Their reaction to it suggested the film was <totally lit/fire/nearly perfect/completely delightful/four and a half stars>
Their reaction to it suggested the film was <a bit of a dud/not so good/difficult to get through/hard to watch/a drag>
They were <amazed/impressed> by the <amount of information/level of entertainment> offered in such a short amount of time.
One of them remarked it's a short film that could easily be made into <an amazing/an epic/a five-star/a classic/a blockbuster> feature-length film.
One follower summed it up by saying it was third on the list of film types: the feature-length film, the short film, and the should have never been made film.

One follower, with a bachelor's degree in film, said the concept was lacking, and the <lighting/sound editing/costume design/set design> was atrocious, but the <acting/cinematography/visual effects/soundtrack/directing> made up for it.
One follower commented that it was a 120-minute film that ran 119 minutes too long.
The entire audience stood and cheered at the end, with one of the followers wildly screaming, "<Five stars/Academy Award/Movie of the year/Best movie ever/I love that movie/Life changing>!".
Throughout the performance you heard an abundance of cheers, laughter, whistles, and applause.
They remarked that the set design was good, but that's about it.
One of them said the stage acting was on par with a <primary school performance/kids playhouse performance/play that's off-off-off Broadway>.
Reviews of the performance were mixed but mostly positive.
They seemed to be more excited about getting ice cream after the production than the actual event itself.
Nobody said a word after the production; they all just stood up and left.
There wasn't a dry eye in the house.
Everyone gave a standing ovation at the end while chanting, "Encore!".
Before it ended, you noticed most of the audience had "gone to the bathroom" and never returned.
Most of them agreed it wasn't bad but <needed more oomph/lacked pizazz/fell a bit short of being great/was missing a certain something/lacked a certain je ne sais quoi>.
After it ended, everyone awkwardly avoided answering the question, "What did you think?".
You kept hearing various levels of snoring throughout the production.
After it ended, nobody wanted to leave, and they started chanting, "Again, Again, Again!".
